title: Bridge wear-in with age
question: Per 5-year age cohort of the 2025 inventory: is ln(share of bridges with lowest rating ≤ 4) a straight line in age from 5 to 44 years, and per material and 10-year age band, is the mean lowest rating of steel bridges below that of prestressed concrete ones at the same age?

issues.text: Age in a single inventory is a cohort difference, not one bridge ageing: older cohorts were built to other standards and the worst were already replaced.
issues.fix: Read the slope as the cross-sectional wear-in of today's stock; the reconstruction clock and the materials at equal age are the checks; annual NBI files would give the panel.

issues.text: The server aggregates: the data are counts per year built and rating, not bridges.
issues.fix: The regression runs on cohorts (5-year bands), weighted implicitly by sizes of 600-47,000 bridges.

issues.text: Overall poor shares per material compare materials of different ages (prestressed concrete averages 35 years, steel 54).
issues.fix: Compare the mean rating within the same 10-year age band (materials step), not the overall share.

alternatives.question: Does the doubling time differ between steel and prestressed concrete cohorts?
alternatives.why: Drills into material; needs counts per material, year built and rating (paged server query).

alternatives.question: Do reconstructed bridges age from the year of reconstruction at the same rate as new ones?
alternatives.why: Drills into item 106; the clocks step has both curves.

alternatives.question: Do average daily traffic, truck share or freeze-thaw climate (state) speed up the wear-in?
alternatives.why: Expands with ADT_029, PERCENT_ADT_TRUCK_109 and STATE_CODE_001 from the same server.

hypotheses.statement: The log share of poor bridges rises linearly with age from 5 to 44 years.
hypotheses.null: The log poor share does not change with age.

hypotheses.statement: At the same age, steel bridges have a lower mean lowest rating than prestressed concrete bridges.
hypotheses.null: Steel and prestressed concrete bridges of the same age rate the same.

concepts.label: Bridge cohort
concepts.description: Bridges built in the same 5-year span (year built, NBI item 27).
concepts.why: The unit the server's counts allow.

concepts.label: Bridge age
concepts.description: 2025 minus year built; the inventory is as of June 2025.

concepts.label: Condition rating
concepts.description: The lowest of the deck, superstructure, substructure and culvert ratings (0-9).

concepts.label: Poor share
concepts.description: Share of a cohort with lowest rating ≤ 4 (FHWA's poor class).

concepts.label: Main-span material
concepts.description: NBI item 43A: concrete, steel, prestressed concrete, timber, masonry, ...
concepts.why: A candidate for different wear rates.

concepts.label: Rating history
concepts.description: Each bridge's rating year by year.
concepts.why: A panel would separate wear from survivor bias and fit Markov transition probabilities.

strategy.detail: FHWA's annual NBI ASCII files 1992-2025, joined on STRUCTURE_NUMBER_008 and STATE_CODE_001.

data.request: Lowest condition rating per bridge and inventory year, 1992-2025
data.why: Year-to-year transitions give the Markov deterioration model without survivor bias.

method.summary: H1: a straight line of log_poor on age_mid over the cohorts aged 5-44 (the hazard step gives the least-squares fit); H2: the means method compares steel and prestressed concrete mean_rating within age bands.

steps.title: Counts per year built and rating
steps.detail: by_rating: the server's count per YEAR_BUILT_027 and LOWEST_RATING.

steps.title: Cohorts and poor share
steps.detail: ratings and cohorts: 5-year age bands, share_poor = bridges with rating ≤ 4 / bridges, log_poor.

steps.title: Fit the wear-in
steps.detail: hazard: log_poor on age_mid for bands 5-40, growth_per_year and doubling_years.

steps.title: Materials
steps.detail: materials: STRUCTURE_KIND_043A codes 1-9 into names, 10-year bands.

steps.title: Steel against prestressed concrete at equal age
steps.detail: means of mean_rating per band for material steel versus prestressed concrete.

steps.title: Accept, reject, or extend to the panel
steps.detail: If the fit bends past 45 years, the bend is maintenance and survivor bias: fetch the annual files.

caveats: One inventory, not bridges followed over time: old cohorts are the survivors.
Ratings are inspectors' judgements on a 0-9 scale every 24 months (some 12 or 48).
The lowest rating of four components hides which one is poor.
Year built is the original construction; item 106 records only the latest reconstruction.
Cohort counts weigh unevenly: the 1906-1910 band has 2,000 bridges, 1966-1970 47,000.
